findings.summary: When options.encoding is configured, the Accept-Encoding header is never checked, so responses get compressed with an encoding the client did not advertise, breaking content negotiation.
Same change as in src: a configured options.encoding bypasses the Accept-Encoding check, so responses are compressed with an encoding the client did not accept.
Substring matching on Accept-Encoding (accepted.includes('gzip')) matches 'gzip;q=0' (a refusal) and does not parse q-values; this flaw already existed in the old regex, so it is not a regression.
